sharedDesignSpecification:
Exactly FOUR ROWS and FOUR COLUMNS: rows top-to-bottom C, B, A, S; columns left-to-right MOBILITY, BALANCED, HEAVY, MAINTENANCE. Exactly sixteen FULL-BODY character figures, one per cell, all feet visible, same camera, same character scale. Label every cell clearly: C1 C2 C3 C4, B1 B2 B3 B4, A1 A2 A3 A4, S1 S2 S3 S4. Large portrait-format high-resolution design poster, generous cell spacing, equipment silhouettes legible, minimal text, no extra figures or missing cells.
Tier garment design language MUST differ across all four roles:
C: scavenged olive/brown/rust orange, soft worn asymmetrical cropped utility vest, coarse diagonal fastening, mismatched small reclaimed steel plates, repaired hems, patched utility shorts.
B: dusty blue-gray/cream/ochre, recognizable rounded civilian PATROL UNIFORM cropped bolero jacket with rounded stand collar, curved lapel protection and big horizontal buckles; rounded split hip overskirt over opaque utility shorts. Not a color swap of C.
A: charcoal/dark olive/brick red, short angular MILITARY COMBAT JACKET with clavicle yoke, angular segmented chest protection, red quick-release tab; independently suspended angular HIP PROTECTION TABS over shorts. Not a recolor of B.
S: cobalt navy/white/silver/restrained cyan, engineered asymmetrical short TECH WAISTCOAT with a split high collar, an open shoulder, thin curved composite rib shells, recessed connectors, short asymmetric HIP COAT-TAILS over opaque shorts; streamlined separate leg shells. Not a recolor of B/A; no magical superhero armor.
Role differentiation within EACH tier must be obvious in silhouette, garment cut and plate arrangement:
Column 1 MOBILITY: smallest, most compact carrier/top variant with open arm joints, minimal hip layers and small pouches, flexible short leg protection; lightweight explorer/scout variant. Keep the tier's specific vest/bolero/jacket/technical-waistcoat identity.
Column 2 BALANCED: the reference standard torso design and medium hip modules, moderate pouches and two normal knee pads. Carry over the balanced costumes shown in the clothing reference.
Column 3 HEAVY: substantially broader LAYERED torso panels, separate articulated shoulder caps that do not crush neck, larger independent hip tabs, elbow/forearm and knee/shin protection, weight visibly supported by harness. Short sleeves/open joints, a visible abdomen or side-waist gap and some upper thigh remain. It must read as a heavy variant of its OWN tier rather than identical heavy armor recolored.
Column 4 MAINTENANCE: distinct cropped service jacket/rolled sleeve or open-shoulder service-harness variant, readily accessible broad release buckles, exposed replaceable armor segments and repair seams, tool-roll at hip, compact rear spare-panel pack, asymmetric service pouches. Prioritize accessible repair/replaceable panels; no medical symbols or healing apparatus. Clearly different silhouette from heavy armor and not just extra ammo pouches.
Same role in different tiers must also remain obviously different through the tier-specific garment cut, neckline, shell segmentation and attachment system. Clothing should fit compact SD bodies, never enlarge or elongate body to fit gear. Preserve practical neck/shoulder/elbow/hip articulation. Preserve original hair color and hairstyle. No helmets, weapons, male mannequins, generic adult fashion model bodies, excessive neon, huge mecha armor, fantasy spikes, sex poses, bikini/lingerie or visible basewear. Secure opaque tops fully cover chest and shorts fully cover pelvis/buttocks. Maintain subculture costume style: bare upper arms/shoulders, modest abdomen or side-waist opening and some upper thigh rather than all-covered jumpsuits. Nonsexual neutral equipment presentation. All 16 must keep the SAME face and original head-to-body proportion. Neutral relaxed arms slightly away from torso, front three-quarter view, clean stylized 3D anime GAME render, neutral gray studio background. Footer "16 DESIGN CONCEPTS / NOT 3D FITTED / APPROVAL REQUIRED".

serin:
Use case: identity-preserve / character-specific costume comparison sheet.
Image1 is the FINAL EDEL sixteen-armor product board: this is the exact equipment-product and 4x4 layout reference. Image2 is the actual SERIN game model: this is the STRICT character identity and body-proportion reference.
Make SERIN's full sixteen-armor board. Replace ALL SIXTEEN EDEL figures with SERIN. Use SERIN's own brown eyes, original BROWN hair, ponytail, facial shape, compact shoulder/torso/hip contours and original large-head/short-limb game proportions from image2. Do not simply recolor Edel's hair or copy Edel's torso; the character must read as the original Serin. Remove the reference gun. Neutral nonsexual equipment presentation.
All sixteen armor products must correspond cell-for-cell with image1: C1 through S4, same garment design, shell pattern, color family, accessories and silhouette identity, with clothing curvature and strap lengths visually adapted to Serin's different body. Keep two separate ideas intact: SAME PRODUCT identities, DIFFERENT CHARACTER fitting concept. This is a 2D concept sheet, not a claim of actual 3D fitting.
EXACT 4 ROW x 4 COLUMN layout. Rows C / B / A / S; columns MOBILITY / BALANCED / HEAVY / MAINTENANCE. Every cell keeps its correct identifier C1 C2 C3 C4, B1 B2 B3 B4, A1 A2 A3 A4, S1 S2 S3 S4. Same camera, gray studio background, generous spacing, same relative framing; all heads and boots fully inside cells. Exactly sixteen SERIN figures with brown ponytail, no lavender-haired figures or mannequins.
Preserve the equipment differences:
C salvaged asymmetric cropped olive/brown vest and rusty reclaimed plates.
B rounded blue-gray/cream patrol jacket/bolero, curved shell/lapels and ochre industrial fasteners.
A charcoal/dark olive military crop jacket, angular plates/hip tabs and brick-red quick releases; no stray blue/white boots.
S navy/white/silver engineered asymmetric tech waistcoat, split collar, curved composite shells, open shoulder and asymmetric hip coat-tail. Especially S2 must match image1's asymmetric S balanced costume, not B2's rounded bolero.
MOBILITY column1: compact open-joint low-bulk variant, few pouches.
BALANCED column2: the standard moderate protection version.
HEAVY column3: broad layered torso/hip panels, separate articulated shoulder caps, distinct forearm and shin guards without crushing neck or changing body proportions.
MAINTENANCE column4: each tier's own cropped service jacket/vest with accessible buckles and replaceable panel seams, visible compact hip TOOL ROLL plus a spare-armor PANEL CARRIER on the other hip/back; asymmetric repair silhouette, no medical equipment. C4 coarse work jacket, B4 rolled blue-gray service bolero/cream rounded pads, A4 olive military engineer short jacket/charcoal-red pads, S4 refined composite spare-panel docking carrier with small tool roll.
Preserve the subculture costume exposure from image1: bare upper arms or shoulders, modest abdomen/side-waist opening and some upper thigh in all four tiers. Secure opaque tops and utility shorts cover chest/pelvis/buttocks; no underwear visible, no lingerie, cleavage focus, nude regions or sexual posing. Do not turn short SD characters into tall adult fashion models. Clothing follows the source character, never elongates the character to match gear.
Title "SERIN / ALL 16 ARMOR DESIGNS".
Keep header role names and all tier row/cell labels.
Footer "16 DESIGN CONCEPTS / NOT 3D FITTED / APPROVAL REQUIRED".
Large sharp portrait-format stylized 3D anime GAME render poster, readable equipment differences.
